💡 Key Takeaways
  • As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking significant.
  • It has been revealed that the company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov.
  • It was a huge moment for SpaceX, bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking significant.

It has been revealed that the company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower.

It was a huge moment for SpaceX, bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship.

In a recent development, "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines.".

The current version of Starship — the one that rolled out Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage.

Industry observers note that V3's Ship is 171 feet (52 m) tall and features six of SpaceX's Raptor V3 engines. (The similarly reusable Super Heavy V3 booster is powered by 33 Raptors.) So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power.

Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon.

Recent findings suggest that even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g.

To provide a little perspective about that vehicle's planned dimensions: The V4 Ship will be the same height as a fully stacked Falcon 9, SpaceX's workhorse two-stage rocket, and much broader: Ship is 30 feet (9 m) across, while the Falcon 9's payload fairing is 17.1 feet (5.2 m) wide.

This isn't the first we've heard about a V4 Starship. Back in August 2025, for example, Musk posted a graphic showing Starship's planned progression from the V2 to the V3 to the V4, which he remarked is expected to debut in 2027.

That slide pegs the future Starship's total height at 466 feet (142 m), 200 feet (61 m) of which would be Ship. But those numbers are out of date, Musk stressed in the post, saying that V4 is "probably closer to 150m height.".

So, yeah: If all goes according to proposal, the next Starship will be nearly 500 feet tall.

It has been revealed that starship V4 will be ~70m long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load. Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher thrust V4 engines.November 16, 2026.

The original Starship Flight 15 mission plan called for a double chopsticks catch, with both Super Heavy and Ship coming back to the launch tower for recovery.

Industry observers note that this would have been feasible, as the catches were scheduled a day apart: Super Heavy would land just 6.5 minutes after launch, while Ship would circle Earth for 22.5 hours, and deploy a batch of SpaceX's Starlink V3 internet satellites, before coming home. (Ship ended up delivering the satellites as planned.).

Recent findings suggest that the twofer didn't happen, however; Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday as a result. But that wasn't a huge deal, as SpaceX had already pulled off Super Heavy catches on three previous Starship flights.

It has been revealed that the Ship catch was unprecedented, because it's been a taller order. Ship returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter. SpaceX hadn't even tried the maneuver before Flight 15, so executing it was a very major deal.

Recent findings suggest that "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot stated during the tech giant's Ship-landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes.".

#13486. Industry News: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1162 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh row over a record-breaking EU loan to European aerospace firm Airbus could reopen a long-standing rift with Washington and threaten an existing EU-US trade truce.
  • The European Investment Bank (EIB), the lending arm of the EU, agreed in June to loan Airbus up to €3 billion ($3.4 billion) but US President Donald Trump's top trade advisor recently suggested the loan breached a 2021 EU-US agreement on state support.
  • "I had sincerely hoped that trade-distorting European subsidies to Airbus were a thing of the past," US Trade Representative Jamieson Grier said in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh row over a record-breaking EU loan to European aerospace firm Airbus could reopen a long-standing rift with Washington and threaten an existing EU-US trade truce.

The European Investment Bank (EIB), the lending arm of the EU, agreed in June to loan Airbus up to €3 billion ($3.4 billion) but US President Donald Trump's top trade advisor recently suggested the loan breached a 2021 EU-US agreement on state support.

"I had sincerely hoped that trade-distorting European subsidies to Airbus were a thing of the past," US Trade Representative Jamieson Grier said in late October. "For decades, France, Germany and Spain have aggressively supported Airbus, their national champion aircraft manufacturer, to gain an unfair advantage over US aerospace workers and business.".

He also suggested there was a lack of transparency around the terms of the loan. The EU insists the loan does not amount to subsidies, that it is in close contact with the Office of the US Trade Representative and "will provide all necessary information," a spokesperson told DW.

An Airbus spokesperson told DW the manufacturer is "actively engaging with the relevant authorities and are happy to share more information about the loan with governments.".

Airbus and the US company Boeing, the world's two largest plane manufacturers, were previously involved in a 17-year corporate trade dispute.

The World Trade Organization (WTO) ruled that both the EU and US provided the companies with state subsidies, resulting in years of tariffs, tit-for-tat retaliation and claims of victory by both sides.

A deal to end tariffs with strict provisions on state support was finally agreed in 2021 and strengthened in 2025, but the latest row threatens to reopen the dispute and could potentially threaten the wider EU-US tariff deal agreed last year, experts say.

The previous Airbus-Boeing dispute was one of the longest-running corporate disputes in history and led to billions of dollars' worth of tariffs leveled by both sides.

"Trade experts tend to hate to talk about it because there are so many ups and downs to the story, it took so long to get resolved and it always tends to creep back up again," Inu Manak, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics who specializes in international trade law and policy, told DW.

She indicates because the matter is such a "persistent thorn in the side," it has the potential to spiral, but for now the US is only signaling displeasure before things escalate. "They want to talk about this, and that conversation will need to happen before anything goes further," she stated.

At the heart of the current dispute is whether the €3 billion loan from the EIB, the largest corporate loan ever authorized by the bank, amounts to illegal state support.

Sources indicate that "The EIB loan to Airbus is a standard loan on market terms," a European Commission spokesperson told DW. "It carries interest, it must be repaid in full, and it is the type of financing the EIB provides every year to companies across many sectors.".

A spokesperson for the bank told DW the €3 billion loan is "a standard EIB corporate loan, implemented under the bank's established procedures and on market-based terms." It indicates it considers the financing to be "fully consistent with the market-terms principle" of the 2021 deal.

A spokesperson for Airbus told DW the loan is "a standard corporate financing facility, similar to commercially available loans we've signed in the past.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Fredrik Erixon, founding director of the European Center for International Political Economy, says the lines are still blurred when it comes to what counts as a subsidy and what is just a loan and that only a comprehensive World Trade Organization investigation could establish the full facts.

Another potential problem is how the €3 billion will be used, including the share earmarked for research and development and how much funding will support defense-related activities versus commercial aircraft development.

Inu Manak says it is impossible at this point to determine if the loan amounts to the provision of illegal subsidies or not, and that it depends on the very specific terms of the credit provided and whether or not it could be proved to be damaging to Boeing's business.

"If it's a market-based loan, if it's not providing below-market rates that would provide an unfair advantage, then it should be fine," she said. "That remains to be seen.".

In Erixon's view, the situation is further complicated by the fact that the aerospace sector is "a highly murky business" due to the amount of defense contracts companies like Boeing and Airbus hold with governments and the high costs associated with that in terms of research and development.

"The problem is we've ended up in a world where there's only two large aircraft manufacturers," he told DW. "And it is a business with high upfront costs when you're going to develop different things.".

He points out that while Boeing may have a legitimate grievance over this loan, Airbus and the EU can point to Boeing's own deals with the US government.

"Boeing does R&D contracts for military purposes, which end up producing technology and support for the civil aircraft program for Boeing," said Erixon. "That's also what the World Trade Organization found previously.".

It was Boeing that originally asked the US trade representative back in July to intervene over the loan, linking it to Airbus' proposal to develop a new single-aisle aircraft program, which could spark a new era of intense competition between the two giants. Neither the US trade representative nor Boeing responded to a DW request for comment.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Inu Manak thinks the next obvious step for the US would be to launch a Section 301 investigation, which is an official inquiry to determine if the loan "violates an international trade agreement or is unjustified, unreasonable or discriminatory, and that burdens or restricts US commerce.".

She thinks the Trump administration has no interest in engaging with the WTO and believes it has the potential to threaten the broader EU-US trade agreement.

"I don't think there's a lot that can stop the US trade representative from taking action if they decide they want to do it," Manak mentioned. "They may think there may be something else to extract from the European Union.".

Fredrik Erixon agrees that "it's going to be a point of leverage that the Americans can use against Europe," adding that the dynamics underpinning the aerospace sector — that both Boeing and Airbus need greater government investment due to ramped-up military spending — is the fundamental underlying problem.

Sources indicate that "We are getting into a state aid race, which basically means these companies just need more and more and more money," he said. "That in itself is an escalatory development.".

Industry News: Culture, defence, Fernandes - Pochettino's priorities at Man Utd

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1388 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United head coach will be at Liverpool on 22 November.
  • "We have to find a way to create the best habits and culture that makes us close to winning every single game.".
  • Mauricio Pochettino has used his first interview as Manchester United head coach to outline his vision for the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United head coach will be at Liverpool on 22 November.

"We have to find a way to create the best habits and culture that makes us close to winning every single game.".

Mauricio Pochettino has used his first interview as Manchester United head coach to outline his vision for the club.

The former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea boss wasted no time getting across the Atlantic Ocean after completing his stint in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

He met key staff on Wednesday, took training for the first time on Thursday and conducts his first wider media conference at United's Carrington training ground on Friday.

The 54-year-old is facing a packed schedule, starting with a trip to Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

According to recent reports, pochettino accepted a big challenge. United are 18th in the table. By 17:00 GMT on Saturday, they could be bottom.

So, what are the Argentine's priorities as he begins the task of trying to transform United's season?

There is a clear non-negotiable.

"To create the culture is the most vital [thing]," he told United's in-house media in a 15-minute introductory chat.

Pochettino's first Man Utd training session filmed by drone operator.

Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino.

Fitness obsessed & 'control freak' - what can Man Utd expect from Pochettino?

Matheus Cunha's injury-time goal against Roma on 3 November sealed one of only three Manchester United victories in 15 games this season.

It would be easy to point to areas of the pitch where United have been deficient this season. However, it cannot be totally dismissed that virtually the same group of players were transformed over the second half of last season by the recently sacked Michael Carrick, who guided them to third in the Premier League and Champions League qualification.

Remarkably, Pochettino has won twice as many matches in charge of the USA this season than the three victories United have managed, with a 100% record from six games.

Industry observers note that united, by contrast, have not won in the Premier League since August, while two of their three victories have required the Red Devils to come from behind. Their single clean sheet came against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah FK in the Champions League in September.

One of the most immediate tasks for Pochettino will be to alter the mindset of players who seem to have become restricted by the pressure they have found themselves subjected to.

"It is a mistake to see the situation," he stated. "We need to see the potential of this club.

"We need to understand it is a game, and to connect with the game we need to feel free. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is our priority now; to work with them and take the pressure.

In a recent development, "Pressure needs to bring energy. Responsibility needs to bring energy because if not, it is too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.".

Diogo Dalot is consoled by Manchester United team-mate Joshua Zirkzee after being substituted during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

That remarked, there are some glaring concerns that Carrick was unable to fix and Pochettino must find an answer to. The most obvious is defence.

Who should the cornerstones of United's defence be?

In a recent development, the Carrick regime felt Leny Yoro was the player with the attributes - pace, strength and control - most suited to their needs. Yet, at 21, Yoro is prone to mistakes and he has also been needed at right-back because regular right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have, at times, been required on the left.

Industry observers note that lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt have not been reliable fitness wise. Pochettino knows the baggage attached to Martinez, given his post-match criticisms of the club hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid, and the knowledge his fellow countryman's contract expires in the summer.

Harry Maguire has started all 10 league games this season but suffered a back spasm in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, immediately before the international break, and had to be replaced at half-time. Maguire has many attributes, but his presence does restrict the ability to press high up the field.

Ayden Heaven has made eight appearances in all competitions but has previously been regarded as being behind Yoro in terms of his overall development.

The 27-year-old was consoled by Joshua Zirkzee when he was replaced against Villa, such was the negative fan reaction to his performance, which included conceding a penalty at the start of the second-half.

It can justifiably be argued if Dalot has the talent to match the 260 club appearances he has now made.

However, for his faults, coaches love his attitude.

Dalot has been described to BBC Sport as having one of the most committed and professional approaches to the game, that he is someone willing to take responsibility, happy to play in unfamiliar positions if it benefits the team, the first to offer support to team-mates, and a positive influence in the dressing room.

Liverpool and Man Utd fans give predictions ahead of Premier League match.

Bruno Fernandes' alarming drop off in form has been one of the most noticeable features of the current campaign.

The Portugal playmaker has been a shadow of the star who scooped all the player of the year awards last season and broke the Premier League assist record.

He was axed for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after criticising Carrick's tactics in the 4-1 Champions League humiliation by Como and seems to be affected by concerns around his future - his contract also expires in the summer, although United are almost certain to trigger their one-year option on the 32-year-old - and the summer arrival of Youri Tielemans.

For the short term at least, Pochettino must decide whether to pick Fernandes in his favoured number 10 role and work around that, or drop him deeper, as Ruben Amorim did, or play him wide, which has not brought the best out of him.

Why does Pochettino keep lemons in his office?

It has been revealed that fernandes' status affects other areas. Carrick never seemed convinced by Andrey Santos, a Â£50m summer arrival from Chelsea. But with Â£70m Carlos Baleba out for an extended period, a partner needs to be found in midfield for Kobbie Mainoo.

Tielemans did not seem to have the running ability for the role, and Amorim wouldn't pick Mainoo with Fernandes.

It has been revealed that further forward, with Benjamin Sesko out, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo have tended to be used in the number nine role. But Cunha likes to drop deep, while, after a bright start to the season, Mbeumo has scored twice in his past 12 appearances.

Sources indicate that neither Shea Lacey nor Harry Amass have started a Premier League game this season. Both caught the eye on England Under-20 duty during the international break. Pochettino has history for giving young players a chance and the pair could benefit from that.

Manchester United co-chair Avram Glazer and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe have been the subject of numerous supporter protests and chants.

There is one issue Pochettino mentioned in his interview he will soon discover requires delicate handling.

Sources indicate that united's match-going fans have stood by every manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired. There is no reason to think that will change now.

Industry observers note that however, their relationship with the club's ownership is fractured, possibly beyond repair. Fresh accounts to 30 September show the club's overall debt remains more than Â£1.1bn and a further Â£14.5m was spent on finance costs in the previous quarter.

This fuels discontent in the stands, already heightened because of various ticketing measures, none of which are viewed by most supporters as being positive.

"We need to be united," said Pochettino.

"Chemistry is really vital, chemistry between us and the staff and the fans and the players, the directors, the owners and everything.".

Relive Starship's historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and 'Mechazilla' tower catch

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (871 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time.
  • Sources indicate that flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov.
  • It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time.

Sources indicate that flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable.

Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did.

Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench.

The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies.

Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II, with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away.

This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling.

Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review.

According to recent reports, A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space, while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase.

Recent findings suggest that that return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase.

Super heavy performed its landing burn above the Gulf of Mexico before cutting its engines for a brief moment and exploding in a giant fireball.

This was an intentional detonation, courtesy of the vehicle's flight termination system.

Recent findings suggest that ship continued on to low Earth orbit, where it deployed a payload of 26 upgraded Starlink Version 3 satellites. It was the second batch of V3 Starlinks delivered during Starship’s recent flight tests, each of which has added what SpaceX notes is the equivalent of 10 Falcon 9 Starlink V2 satellite debuts worth of data capacity to its orbital constellation.

Flight 15 was also Starship's second-ever mission to orbit, and its longest so far. Ship spent nearly a full day in orbit, circling Earth a total of 14 times. During its jaunt in space, the spacecraft cleared three separate check points, which allowed SpaceX the opportunity to divert the vehicle for an ocean splashdown if needed, and finally was given the green light to attempt the first-ever Ship tower catch.

According to recent reports, at approximately 4:18 p.m. EST (2018 GMT, 3:18 p.m. local time in Texas) on Saturday (Nov. 14), the spacecraft broke through the cloud cover that blanketed the skies above Starbase as onlookers watched its bellyflop plunge toward the ground. Moments after becoming visible, Ship ignited its engines for a flip and burn maneuver, which oriented it upright and swung its trajectory into the tightening grip of the chopstick arms of Starbase's "Mechazilla" launch tower.

After a slight sway back and forth suspended above Earth in Mechazilla's embrace, Ship came to a complete rest, hanging motionless as a historic milestone in SpaceX’s pursuit of fully reusable spaceflight.

It hung there overnight as engineers, and even SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, inspected the spacecraft. Ship was lowered on Sunday (Nov. 15) and transported back to SpaceX's Starbase hanger bay for further checkouts.

SpaceX has not yet said whether Ship 42 will fly again, but its return gives engineers a chance to examine how the spacecraft held up through launch, nearly a day in orbit and atmospheric reentry.

Those findings will help inform upcoming flights as SpaceX ramps up production to continue testing Starship's capabilities.

Josh Dinner is Space.com's Spaceflight Staff Writer and a photographer with a passion for science and exploration. He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram, and follow him on X, where he mostly posts in haiku.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J.
  • According to recent reports, science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) finds.
  • Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J. Richards/AFP via Getty.

According to recent reports, science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine (NASEM) finds. Standards for fixing errors are also inconsistently applied across research journals, it indicates.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science.

There are no data on how long retraction or correction currently takes, as journals do not generally disclose when they were alerted to a problem in a paper; the NASEM report indicates they should. On average, according to the Retraction Watch database, retractions occur around 2.4 years after a paper is published. The report recommends that editorial review processes be completed within 12 weeks for most cases and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months — at least when editors are looking at concerns over a single paper.

Sources indicate that “The big picture is, the process is too slow,” states Randy Schekman, a cell biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, who chaired the 14-person committee that produced the NASEM report. A prompter and more transparent process would strengthen the reliability of the scientific record, he says.

The report was due to be published online on 19 November, but publication was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained some references with fabricated first names for authors, a possible sign that large language models had been used to write or edit the material and had been insufficiently checked.

“It's unfortunate that there were these flawed references in a report about fixing the literature,” notes Jennifer Byrne, a cancer researcher and research integrity sleuth at the University of Sydney who first flagged the concern to Science when reviewing the report, which was shared ahead of publication with media outlets.

Sources indicate that the report had two main aims: to speed up the process of retraction or correction and to lower the “tremendous emotional barriers” for authors to correct honest mistakes in the record, Schekman says. “Part of the problem is that it’s too rare for a paper to be retracted,” he adds.

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Recent findings suggest that the report also suggests that journals shouldn’t just wait for complaints to reach them, but instead “take proactive steps” to identify errors and integrity challenges. That might include journal-wide audits, or regularly monitoring social media and online platforms where post-publication issues are raised, it notes.

Existing guidelines for publishers, such as those from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in London, only urge a “timely” response to concerns without setting out expected schedules, and don’t suggest journals scan online platforms for complaints.

Recent findings suggest that “A major theme running through the report is that we have to distinguish between retraction or correction, and research misconduct,” notes Dorothy Bishop, a research-integrity sleuth in Oxford, UK, who was on the NASEM committee. Authors shouldn’t associate retracting a paper with the stigma of misconduct, she notes. And although journal editors sometimes wait for a university to investigate whether there is research misconduct before correcting a paper, they shouldn’t, she adds.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a upcoming record.

Recent findings suggest that calls for changing these attitudes aren’t new: journals have long emphasized that retractions can cover honest mistakes. When it comes to journal processes, Holden Thorpe, the editor in chief of Science, urged that issuing corrections or retractions and making a determination of misconduct be separated in an editorial in 2022, and COPE guidelines already emphasize the point. But “there are still plenty of people who see a correction or retraction as an allegation of fraud,” says Thorpe, who was also on the NASEM committee. “Hopefully, this report will accelerate the recognition of the distinction,” he says.

Arsenal 'have ingredients' but Europe's elite on another level

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez made six saves but was beaten twice in defeat by Lyon.
  • It is only 18 months since Arsenal tasted European glory, but they are not a team on many people's list of favourites for this season's Women's Champions League.
  • That is because not only have the Gunners disappointed across their opening 15 matches of the season, but also the elite teams in Europe seem to have gone up another level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez made six saves but was beaten twice in defeat by Lyon.

It is only 18 months since Arsenal tasted European glory, but they are not a team on many people's list of favourites for this season's Women's Champions League.

That is because not only have the Gunners disappointed across their opening 15 matches of the season, but also the elite teams in Europe seem to have gone up another level.

In the space of seven days, Arsenal have witnessed first hand what it takes to reach those heights - and the gap they must bridge.

Last week, they were resilient at Barcelona to earn a very respectable 1-1 draw, but were fortunate the Spanish side were not clinical with their chances at Camp Nou.

On Thursday night, they were outplayed at home in losing 2-0 to an excellent Lyon side, who look on course to match or better their runner-up finish from last season.

One point from such games could be pleasing - but that only demonstrates the work Arsenal need to do to be considered one of the top teams in Europe.

French giants Lyon outclass Arsenal in Women's Champions League.

Arsenal came into Thursday's defeat by Lyon off the back of a fifth successive Women's Super League draw at Emirates Stadium against London City Lionesses.

In contrast, Lyon have been flying domestically, winning all nine of their matches, scoring 49 goals, and then not conceding any in their unbeaten Champions League run.

Such form sets the pace and it was clear at Meadow Park that they were superior to Arsenal in every department.

Vibrant Germany international Jule Brand gave them the lead midway through the first half and Melchie Dumornay sealed the win with a powerful strike in the 57th minute.

Arsenal defender Leah Williamson remarked the "better team won the game" and manager Renee Slegers highlighted the difference in physicality between the teams.

Recent findings suggest that "Compared to last year when we played Lyon [in the semi-finals], they are even better now. They have standout individual quality," Slegers noted.

It has been revealed that "They dominated in the first half. We had solutions for the second half and had more presence. We wore them down better but it still didn't lead to open chances.".

Despite playing at right-back, Jule Brand had the third most touches in the Arsenal penalty area for Lyon (five) after striker Marie-Antoinette Katoto and fellow goalscorer Melchie Dumornay.

In a recent development, lyon had a 3.33 expected goals ratio on Thursday, serving up 23 shots to Arsenal's seven. They created six big chances and 14 of their shots were inside the box.

Dumornay oozed quality, midfielder Lily Yohannes showed composure and Brand was very impressive both defensively and going forward for Lyon, deployed in a upcoming position.

Those individuals have benefitted from the expertise of former Barcelona manager Jonatan Giraldez, who joined in June 2025 - the month after Arsenal won the Champions League - and has now had the time he needed to impose his style.

As a result, Lyon have gone up another level and the gap between these two teams has widened by Arsenal's drop-off this season.

Slegers also said Arsenal had "prepared all we could" for the intensity that Lyon brought in London - but it still did not have an impact.

Asked how far off Lyon they currently are, Slegers stated: "It's 2-0 today and they are better than us but it doesn't mean if we were to play them again soon, this season, that it would be the same game again.

"We saw moments where we did well and we know from the last couple of years we can hurt Lyon.

"But for today, their pace and physicality helped them get too much dominance in the game and that is one of their strengths. Then it became hard for us.".

Arsenal have not yet qualified for the knockout stages of the Champions League.

Williamson mentioned Arsenal "know what they need to do to be better" and that they are aware of "where the gaps are" to Europe's elite.

They are already 12 points off the pace in the Women's Super League title race and are unlikely to qualify automatically for the Champions League quarter-finals.

"The level rises year on year. Everybody cops goals - we have to try not to and we have to create," mentioned Williamson following the defeat by Lyon.

"We're all focused and we're all together. That's the most comforting thing for me - but this has been a tough period.".

It has not all been bad despite disappointing results - and context is important.

Over a gruelling seven days, they have faced European holders Barcelona, WSL high-flyers London City Lionesses and record Champions League winners Lyon.

They highlighted grit and resilience out in Barcelona last week - traits that have not been on show enough for Arsenal this season, but are clearly there.

Players like Williamson, striker Alessia Russo and summer signings Georgia Stanway and Ona Batlle know what it takes to compete at the highest level.

Arsenal invested in the summer transfer window and brought in proven, experienced players, but that has not translated into results - yet.

Giraldez mentioned time with his players has helped improve Lyon and perhaps that is what Arsenal need - patience.

Recent findings suggest that "I think they are changing now. They made a good game against Barcelona and it's very difficult to go there and get a point," said Giraldez.

Industry observers note that "The game against London City was much better. It's not just about them, but also about us. Now we have improved and play better football than last year.

"I think it is a matter of time [for Arsenal]. They have a good coach and good players. In general, they have all the ingredients to have a good season.".

#13475. Latest Update: How Premier League's significant six keep getting richer

Latest Update: How Premier League's significant six keep getting richer

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'massive six' clubs.
  • Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.
  • In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top five places are occupied by 'massive six' clubs.

Only second-placed Brighton, a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton, have muscled their way in.

In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.

The six biggest clubs - Manchester United, Liverpool, Manchester City, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea - now generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the division's other teams.

And the gap is growing. Every season.

BBC Sport breaks down how the finances of the major six have exploded, examines new trends and the impact on the transfer market, and asks how much it really matters.

Industry observers note that companies put their money where supporters are prepared to spend it. It is a simple fact of business in every country, a reality of football's food chain.

In England, Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester United traditionally dominated viewing figures, column inches, shirt sales and sponsorship.

Over the past 20 years they have been joined by Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham.

This group of clubs now generate so much money it is hard to imagine how they can fail in the long term - even factoring in short-term performance issues.

Let's look at how the gap has grown.

We will use Everton, the only club not in the big six to be in the Premier League since its inception in 1992.

This tells a tale of how even one of the league's founding members can be left trailing well behind.

Sources indicate that in 2009-10, the gap in revenues between the big-six average and Everton was Â£120m. In 2024-25, that gap had grown to Â£442m.

So what has driven this huge escalation?

In large part it is the boom in international TV rights.

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool, told BBC Sport that it has attracted companies prepared to pay large sums to be associated with the Premier League's top clubs.

"The big football brand clubs have global fanbases and that makes them very attractive to global commercial partners, especially for sponsorship and front-of-shirt deals," Maguire stated.

"You combine that with the fact that the Premier League is broadcast to 190 different countries around the world, and especially the international audiences - that allows the clubs to negotiate very good prices.".

Only 10% of Everton's revenue comes from commercial deals, while for the significant six it is 45%.

It means Everton, and other clubs in the league, are heavily reliant on broadcast income. It makes up 66% of their revenue.

For Everton at least, this should change following the move to Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But that is unlikely to be enough to stop the gap increasing.

It has taken a few years, but Aston Villa and Newcastle have begun to increase their revenue.

This is largely thanks to the financial rewards of Champions League football.

But even Uefa has created a system which entrenches the position of the biggest clubs.

When the European Super League initiative was torpedoed, Uefa created a newly introduced financial deal called the value pillar.

This reserves 35% of all Champions League revenues, or Â£713m, for the historically most successful clubs.

Industry observers note that at the end of the league phase last season City are estimated to have earned Â£37.9m from the value pillar, Liverpool Â£35.5m and Chelsea Â£33.3m. Newcastle received only Â£13.6m.

The good news for Villa is their coefficient has improved greatly, aided by last season's Europa League win.

It has been revealed that their value pillar is projected to be worth Â£25m this season. But that will still be less than the substantial six clubs in the competition.

The cards are stacked against an ambitious club - not just domestically, but in Europe too.

Take a look at the financial trend of the massive six and one thing becomes noticeable - Chelsea are beginning to fall behind.

In the past two seasons, and for the first time in recent history, the Blues recorded the lowest revenues of the major six.

Sources indicate that not just by a small amount. They were Â£74m behind Tottenham, and Â£200m below Liverpool and Manchester City.

City's matchday income is the lowest, with the club's huge revenues largely due to commercial deals.

City, however, have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18, inflating the value by using "sham contracts" with sponsors.

The club deny wrongdoing and have lodged an appealed against the verdict.

Chelsea's problem is simple - seats.

According to recent reports, stamford Bridge has a capacity of only 40,000, with no easy scope for expansion. The rest of the big six have grounds which hold at least 60,000.

Chelsea generated an average spend per fan of Â£80 in 2024-25, the second highest in the league after Arsenal.

Yet with 20,000 fewer tickets sold than their big six rivals, Chelsea's total matchday revenues are dwarfed.

Recent findings suggest that "Matchday spend has become increasingly key," Maguire remarked. "There has been a flatlining of broadcast revenues, especially since 2017.

"As a consequence, clubs have had to look at alternative methods of increasing revenues, especially with costs both on the pitch and off pitch rising so fast.".

In a recent development, matchday revenue has effectively stalled for Chelsea, rising only Â£16m over the past 10 years. United's has grown by Â£69m and Spurs, thanks to their fresh ground, by Â£85m.

It has been revealed that "Chelsea are far more reliant upon player sales," Maguire mentioned. "There is a growing divide because the global appeal is very much aligned with three or four clubs.

Industry observers note that "Arsenal have re-established themselves with their progress in the Champions League. Manchester United are a brand in their own right. And Liverpool have expanded Anfield from 44,000 to 61,000, with many of those extra seats having gone to commercial.".

Chelsea's successful player trading model has so far limited the impact.

But there are signs that, financially at least, the major six could become the big five.

You might recall that Villa and Newcastle were not fans of the old profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

PSR forced both clubs to sell some of their best players to balance the books.

That has changed this season with squad-cost ratio (SCR).

Recent findings suggest that there is a key difference with SCR, in that it allows a club to spend the money they generate on players. PSR limited losses so was more restrictive.

Recent findings suggest that "This does make it a little easier for the likes of Villa and Newcastle to spend money," Maguire said. "But it is still heavily weighted in favour of the big six.

In a recent development, "SCR is different to PSR rather than better. For some people, change is advantageous. For others, it isn't.".

It has been revealed that the major six generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the other clubs. So they can spend hundreds of millions of pounds more on their squads.

This makes the massive six even more powerful in the transfer market.

"Look at the clubs who voted against SCR - Brighton, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Fulham and Leeds," Maguire said.

"It's very noticeable that those clubs have traditionally been very good at player sales, while they have tended to have lower matchday and commercial revenues.".

Most of the major six - the outlier being Chelsea - are not remotely close to the Premier League's 85% SCR limit.

Sources indicate that if you give clubs more money to spend on transfers, the likelihood is they will do just that. And the numbers back that up.

Premier League clubs spent Â£3.5bn - not only a highest total for a summer window, but it almost smashed the record for a whole season, the Â£3.53bn set in 2025-26.

The annual accounting cost of previous transfers, or amortisation, has been rising year on year.

"Over the course of the last decade, transfer amortisation has more than doubled and close to tripled," Maguire noted.

"Which means that on average, clubs in the Premier League are now spending, or now have a cost which goes into their SCR calculations of just under Â£100m.".

Uefa fears that SCR will make matters worse, and have an inflationary impact across Europe.

And you can see why it is concerned.

In the summer 13 Premier League clubs broke their transfer record.

Brentford, Brighton, Palace, Leeds and Nottingham Forest all spent more than Â£40m on a player - unthinkable until recently.

So we have learned that the massive six have more money than ever, and the gap is so huge it is impossible for any other club to compete with them, financially at least.

And this is an important point: other than Villa and Newcastle, the other clubs are not trying to compete with the massive six.

Clubs like Brentford and Brighton have shown that smart models are just as effective as fat wallets.

They sign the potential stars of the future, nurture them and then sell them to the big six.

Football's ecosystem recycles the big-six money through the transfer market.

But it is a precarious business for these other clubs.

"The smaller clubs have to get it right on a more regular basis than the bigger clubs," Maguire noted.

"The big six can afford to make signings which are Â£60m and Â£70m, who turn out to be relative flops, and still have those players on high wages for several years.".

And this is perhaps the key point about the vast finances of the big six.

The commercial power of the big six does not guarantee success. After all, United sit in the relegation zone.

Yet Mauricio Pochettino, their fresh manager, may well get the chance to revamp the squad despite the club spending Â£945m on players in the past five years.

Recent findings suggest that the richest clubs can try to spend their way out of trouble. Again and again.

But the rest of the league are only a couple of bad transfer windows from catastrophe.

And that is the real gap between the significant six and the rest.

Anime has never been bigger, and if you have been meaning to catch up on fall simulcasts or plow through a backlog of classics, Crunchyroll just kicked off a rare Black Friday sale that makes signing up a whole lot cheaper.

Unlike streaming promos that only discount the cheapest base tier, Crunchyroll has slashed U.S. prices across all three of its membership levels — Fan, Mega Fan, and Ultimate Fan.

Normally $9.99 per month, the entry-level Fan tier drops to $3.99 per month for your first six months — saving you $6 every month, or $36 total.

It covers all the essentials if you are only watching for yourself: ad-free streaming across Crunchyroll's anime library (note that intends may still include brief trailers or promotional messages before playback), new episodes shortly after they air in Japan, HD downloads for offline viewing, and streaming on 1 device at a time.

If you share an account or want extra gaming and shopping perks, Mega Fan drops from its usual $13.99 per month down to $5.99 per month for six months — saving you $8 a month, or $48 over the promo period.

Mega Fan includes everything in the Fan tier, bumps simultaneous streaming up to 4 devices at once, and unlocks access to Crunchyroll Game Vault (a library of 100+ mobile games with no ads or in-app purchases) besides access to exclusive Crunchyroll Store drops and free U.S. shipping on orders of $50 or more.

Crunchyroll's top-tier Ultimate Fan blueprint is also cut in half for six months, dropping from $17.99 per month to $8.99 per month — saving you $9 each month, or $54 total.

Along with everything in Mega Fan, Ultimate Fan lets you stream on up to 6 devices at the same time, unlocks Crunchyroll Manga access in select countries (with ad-free reading on iOS, Android, and crunchyroll.com/manga for series like The Apothecary Diaries, My Dress-Up Darling, and Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World-, which Mega Fan members can also add separately), gives you free shipping on all Crunchyroll Store orders with no minimum, grants early access to drops, and includes an exclusive swag bag after 12 consecutive months of membership.

It has been revealed that alongside the subscription discounts, Crunchyroll is running several U.S. holiday promotions through the Crunchyroll Store throughout November (most geared toward Mega Fan and Ultimate Fan members, though gift cards are open to everyone):.

Discounted subscription gift cards (Nov. 19-30) — Available to both members and non-members if you want to gift a membership to someone else.

Free Bleach Funko Pop (Nov. 19-24) — Included with Crunchyroll Store purchases over $100, while supplies last.

Free Frieren collectible (Nov. 25-30) — Included with Crunchyroll Store purchases over $100, while supplies last.

On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that they did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico.
  • It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that on Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.

Sources indicate that they did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster. The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA.

It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute.

Recent findings suggest that "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's.".

The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University.

The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI.

As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13.

The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also beamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008.

Shania Twain is standing up for others in country music.

The legendary star in the genre used her acceptance speech for the Equal Play Award at Sunday’s CMT Awards to call for more equity and diversity in the country music industry.

“When I wrote the phrase ‘Man I feel like a woman’ I honestly had no idea at the time it would become an undercurrent of a decades-long career,” she mentioned, referring to one of her biggest hits. “It’s amazing how one statement can empower so many.”.

The phrase, Twain said, “has been adopted by an array of fantastic communities all around the world and become a genuine path of power…which brings me so much joy.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I believe in an all-inclusive country music. We’re family,” Twain remarked. “This is a genre of music with a rich history that raised and nurtured my own songwriting and performance and recording career from childhood. Currently, the industry standard does a real disservice to this.”.

Twain, who was presented the award by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, shouted out some of the diverse acts she is spotlighting on her “Queen of Me” tour this year, including Lily Rose, Lindsay Ell, Hailey Whitters, Mickey Guyton and others.

Industry observers note that “I will continue to do my best as a trailblazer,” Twain said. “Together, let’s ensure all our fellow artists get equal play regardless of gender, age or race.”.

It has been revealed that she also performed acappella with the African American singing group, The BoykinZ, while presenting an award onstage. Twain connected with the group, who are sisters and rising country stars, after Kelly Clarkson surprised them recently by bringing Twain out to meet them during an episode of Clarkson’s daytime talk show.

"Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.

Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.

In a recent development, "Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp said, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves.".

The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.

According to recent reports, it paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

The 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.

"I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp said after the Netherlands match.

In a recent development, "We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired.".

That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.

Industry observers note that but Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.

"They can both play, my goodness," remarked Klopp.

Industry observers note that scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

Recent findings suggest that "A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still said it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.

"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong.".

Recent findings suggest that proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he remarked, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer.".

While that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

Industry observers note that "We've been through a tough time," he stated. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it.".

Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.

Sources indicate that "We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he said.

Industry observers note that in Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

  • A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.
  • Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting racist abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on 15 August last year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Antoine Semenyo was playing for Bournemouth when the alleged incident happened during a match against Liverpool in August 2025.

A Liverpool fan accused of racially abusing footballer Antoine Semenyo has been found not guilty after the player withdrew his support for the prosecution.

Semenyo was due to give evidence at Liverpool Magistrates' Court in the trial of Mark Mogan, 47, who was accused of shouting racist abuse during the opening match of the Premier League season at Anfield on 15 August last year.

But Simon Jones, prosecuting, mentioned: "Following recent contact made with Mr Semenyo, he has indicated he is no longer supportive of proceedings and the prosecution do not consider it is appropriate to compel him.

"In those circumstances we offer no further evidence in the case.".

District Judge Mary Dowrick recorded a verdict of not guilty to the charge of racially aggravated behaviour.

Semenyo, who was a Bournemouth player at the time of the incident but is now signed for Manchester City, had been due to give evidence last month but the trial was adjourned halfway through when Mogan was taken to hospital after suffering a seizure.

Mark Mogan was accused of shouting abuse at Semenyo as he prepared to take a throw in.

The court had heard that Mogan, in a wheelchair, shouted at Semenyo as he went to take a throw-in about 30 minutes into the game.

As he was preparing to take the throw-in Mogan allegedly shouted a racist insult.

Opening the case last month, Jones remarked: "That racial abuse was shouted directly at Antoine Semenyo, who was close to him.

"Mr Semenyo briefly froze, as he couldn't believe what the male had said.".

Witnesses also said they saw him throw his chewing gum at the footballer.

Semenyo reported the incident to the match referee and Mogan was removed from the stadium at half-time.

Mogan, who had an intermediary with him in court, told police in an interview that Semenyo had called him a cripple after he shouted at the player to "hurry up".

Mogan, of Templehill Close in Dovecot, Liverpool, declined to comment as he left court.

#13467. Latest Update: Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (700 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (700 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.
  • That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that right now circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers).
  • According to recent reports, the results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.

That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that right now circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town.

According to recent reports, the results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak. Although the researchers specifically focused on the U.K., they say that such heavy satellite traffic flows above most of Europe, the U.S. and other mid-latitude regions, especially between 40 and 50 degrees north or south.

It has been revealed that "Most Starlink satellites orbit at around 53 degrees to the equator, so the satellites bunch up over the mid-latitudes. These worldwide figures are approximate, based on a global grid over a single day," Accu Components spokesperson told Space.com in an email. "Skies near the equator are the quietest, with around 490 satellites.".

Not all of those satellites are visible to the naked eye, the researchers said in a statement. Because satellites unlike stars don't produce their own light, they must be illuminated by the sun, while the ground below has already sunk into darkness, to be visible. According to the study, an average of 105 satellites out of those 710 were catching light as they zoomed overhead, shining as bright as stars.

Sources indicate that the spokesperson said that the actual number of visible satellites varies drastically throughout the night. During the hours after dusk and before dawn, a much greater number of satellites can be seen, while in the middle of the night most no longer catch any light.

According to recent reports, "For a typical U.K. town, around 300 satellites are catching the sunlight in the first hour or so after dark," the spokesperson said. "That falls to fewer than 20 around midnight, then climbs back to around 300 before dawn.".

Industry observers note that for comparison, as little as a few dozen stars are visible to the naked eye in the dead of the night above large, light-polluted megalopolis such as London or Upcoming York, according to OwnStarMap. In suburban areas and smaller towns, that number grows to a few hundred. To get to a few thousand visible stars, one must retreat into remote countryside or isolated mountain ranges.

The number of satellites orbiting Earth has grown steeply in the past decade, especially since Elon Musk’s SpaceX began launching its internet-beaming Starlink constellation. Satellite companies proposal to launch hundreds of thousands, possibly millions of satellites in the coming decades. If those visions come to pass, the number of passing satellites will vastly outgrow that of stars almost anywhere in the world. The trend especially concerns astronomers who fear the impacts on humankind’s ability to study the Universe.

Recent findings suggest that satellites crossing the view of ground-based telescopes leave streaks in astronomical images and increase the overall brightness of the sky through the light they reflect down towards Earth. Gradually, even the most powerful telescopes could lose their ability to see the distant stars and galaxies that hold the answers to key questions about the history of the universe.

It has been revealed that the study found that throughout the night, an average U.K. town sees 12,891 different satellites passing overhead.

Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

American Airlines noted Wednesday it's bringing small, fresh "bites" to first class on flights between its hubs in New York and Chicago, the carrier's latest effort to win over higher-spending customers.

In a recent development, the changes start this month. Customers will be able to pick between two options, which include prosciutto and melon or apple cinnamon chia pudding for breakfast and a Thai noodle salad or mezze plate for lunch and dinner, American said Wednesday.

In a recent development, american last offered fresh food for first class on these routes in 2019, a spokeswoman said. At the moment, customers in first class on these flights get a smaller, packaged snack. Airlines largely have limited food options for shorter flights, even in first class.

American has fallen behind Delta Air Lines and United Airlines in profits and investments in premium options. The airline has been working to step up those premium offerings in recent years with fresh cabins, lounges and prepares for seatback screens on its narrow-body fleets.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, noted: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner.".

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Read more on the five contenders and cast your vote below.

According to recent reports, sorry, this vote cannot be loaded. In order to vote you need to enable JavaScript in your browser.

Meet the SPOTY Men's Footballer of the Year contenders.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Midfield.

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted manufacturer as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

Bellingham was recently joined in the England squad by his brother Jobe.

Club: Bayern Munich Position: Forward.

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Industry observers note that kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Kane scored his first England goal 79 seconds into his debut in 2015.

Club: Real Madrid Position: Forward.

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Mbappe has won eight consecutive league golden boots.

Club: Barcelona Position: Midfield.

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Rodri scored the goal that won Manchester City the Champions League in 2023.

Club: Barcelona Position: Forward.

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

Lamine Yamal was 16 years and 362 days when he scored at the European Championship in 2024.

Industry observers note that if any of these groups sound like you or someone you know, you've been exposed to the granola lifestyle. Similar to gorpcore, folks who fit the granola aesthetic are typically into camping, hiking, and kayaking, and have probably talked about moving to Colorado one day (guilty). For many, getting into nature was a direct response to feeling cooped up during the lockdowns of the early pandemic. But that trend is here to stay.

For people who are unsure about adventure gear themselves but still want to find the perfect granola gift this holiday season, we chatted with outdoor expert and REI soft goods Lead and Virtual Outfitter Mike Kreis for some outdoor gear shopping tips.

It has been revealed that kreis suggests that you consider how long your giftee has been into their activity, whether it's hiking, skiing, camping, or climbing. "The longer they have been doing the activity, the more gear they will have," he claims.

If your gift recipient already owns some gear, Kreis notes it's best to go for nonessentials. "I always like to go with items that aren't necessarily needed for the activity, as they most likely have that," he says. So opt for a portable charger, a cozy outdoor blanket, or extra camp cooking gadgets. Really, anything that can make outdoor life more comfortable will make a great gift.

If you find yourself shopping for the outdoorsy person in your life, look no further. We've rounded up 30 of the best presents out there, whether their version of adventure is having a picnic in the park or roughing it in the back country.
